units.zh: 梁書卷第三十九 列傳第三十三
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 39, Biography 33
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 39, Biography 33

units.zh: 元法僧 元樹 元願達 王神念 楊華 羊侃 子鶤 羊鴉仁
units.en: Yuan Faseng; Yuan Shu; Yuan Yuanda; Wang Shenian; Yang Hua; Yang Kan; his son Kun; Yang Yaren
units.literal: Yuan Faseng; Yuan Shu; Yuan Yuanda; Wang Shenian; Yang Hua; Yang Kan; his son Kun; Yang Yaren

units.zh: 元法僧，魏氏之支屬也。
units.en: Yuan Faseng belonged to a cadet line of Northern Wei.
units.literal: Yuan Faseng was a collateral branch of the Wei house.

units.zh: 其始祖道武帝。
units.en: His line traced back to Emperor Daowu.
units.literal: His founding ancestor was Emperor Daowu.

units.zh: 父鐘葵，江陽王。
units.en: His father Zhongkui held the title Prince of Jiangyang.
units.literal: His father was Zhongkui, Prince of Jiangyang.

units.zh: 法僧仕魏，歷光祿大夫，後爲使持節、都督徐州諸軍事、徐州刺史，鎮彭城。
units.en: In Wei service he reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then held full staff authority as area commander of Xuzhou forces, inspector of Xuzhou, with his seat at Pengcheng.
units.literal: Faseng served Wei, rose through Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and later became Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Xuzhou, Inspector of Xuzhou, and garrisoned Pengcheng.

units.zh: 普通五年，魏室大亂，法僧遂據鎮稱帝，誅鋤異己，立諸子爲王，部署將帥，欲議匡復。
units.en: When Putong year 5 brought chaos to Wei, Faseng took his post, crowned himself, purged rivals, made his sons kings, and arrayed commanders for a campaign to restore the throne.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Putong the Wei house fell into great disorder; Faseng seized his garrison, declared himself emperor, executed and uprooted dissenters, enfeoffed his sons as kings, deployed generals and commanders, and intended to discuss restoring the dynasty.

units.zh: 旣而魏亂稍定，將討法僧。
units.en: As Wei’s turmoil subsided, the court turned to punish Faseng.
units.literal: Before long the Wei disorder eased somewhat, and they were about to attack Faseng.

units.zh: 法僧懼，乃遣使歸款，請爲附庸，高祖許焉，授侍中、司空，封始安郡公，邑五千戶。
units.en: Terrified, Faseng sent envoys to swear allegiance and ask for protected status. Emperor Wu agreed, made him Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, and created him Duke of Shian with five thousand households.
units.literal: Faseng was afraid and sent envoys to submit in good faith, asking to become a vassal; Emperor Wu assented, appointing him Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, enfeoffing him as Duke of Shian commandery with a fief of five thousand households.

units.zh: 及魏軍旣逼，法僧請還朝，高祖遣中書舍人朱异迎之。
units.en: As Wei troops closed in, Faseng begged to come south; the emperor sent Zhu Yi of the Secretariat to receive him.
units.literal: When Wei armies had already pressed close, Faseng asked to return to court; Emperor Wu dispatched Zhu Yi, Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat for Drafting, to welcome him.

units.zh: 旣至，甚加優寵。
units.en: On arrival he was showered with honors.
units.literal: Once he arrived, he was greatly favored and indulged.

units.zh: 時方事招攜，撫悅降附，賜法僧甲第女樂及金帛，前後不可勝數。
units.en: The court was wooing turncoats, and Faseng received mansions, musicians, gold, and silk beyond counting.
units.literal: At the time they were actively recruiting and reassuring defectors; he was granted mansions, female musicians, gold and silk—countless gifts before and after.

units.zh: 法僧以在魏之日，久處疆埸之任，每因寇掠，殺戮甚多，求兵自衛，詔給甲仗百人，出入禁闥。
units.en: Years on the border in Wei service had left him with many enemies from raiding; he asked for a guard, and the throne gave him a hundred armored men and access to the inner palace.
units.literal: Because during his Wei days Faseng had long held frontier duties and in every raid had killed many, he requested troops for self-protection; an edict granted him a hundred sets of armor and weapons, with leave to enter and leave the inner palace gates.

units.zh: 大通二年，加冠軍將軍。
units.en: In Datong year 2 he was made General of the Champion.
units.literal: In the second year of Datong he was promoted to General of the Champion.

units.zh: 中大通元年，轉車騎將軍。
units.en: Zhongdatong year 1 brought promotion to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

units.zh: 四年，進太尉，領金紫光祿。
units.en: In the fourth year he advanced to Grand Commandant and concurrently held the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Ornament.
units.literal: In the fourth year he advanced to Grand Commandant and concurrently held Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Ornament.

units.zh: 其年，立爲東魏主，不行，仍授使持節、散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、開府同三司之儀、郢州刺史。
units.en: The same year he was named sovereign of Eastern Wei—a title he never exercised—yet kept staff authority, Regular Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Three-Duke ceremonial rank with an open office, and the Yingzhou inspectorate.
units.literal: That year he was installed as ruler of Eastern Wei but did not take it up; still he received Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, privileges equal to the Three Dukes with an open office, and the post of Inspector of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 大同二年，徵爲侍中、太尉，領軍師將軍，薨，時年八十三。
units.en: Datong year 2 recalled him as Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant with the Army Instructor generalship; he died at eighty-three.
units.literal: In the second year of Datong he was summoned as Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, concurrently Army Instructor General; he died at the age of eighty-three.

units.zh: 二子景隆、景仲，普通中隨法僧入朝。
units.en: His sons Jinglong and Jingzhong followed him to Liang during Putong.
units.literal: He had two sons, Jinglong and Jingzhong, who in Putong accompanied Faseng to court.

units.zh: 景隆封沌陽縣公，邑千戶，出爲持節、都督廣越交桂等十三州諸軍事、平南將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
units.en: Jinglong became Duke of Dunyang with a thousand-household fief, then went south as staff-bearing commander over thirteen provinces, General Who Pacifies the South, Pacifier of Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
units.literal: Jinglong was enfeoffed Duke of Dunyang county with a fief of one thousand households and sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in the thirteen provinces of Guang, Yue, Jiao, Gui, and others, General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector General Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 中大通三年，徵侍中、安右將軍。
units.en: Zhongdatong year 3 brought him back as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Right.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Right.

units.zh: 四年，爲征北將軍、徐州刺史，封彭城王，不行，俄除侍中、度支尚書。
units.en: Year 4 made him General Who Campaigns North and Xuzhou inspector and Prince of Pengcheng, though he never went; shortly he was Palace Attendant and Minister of Revenue instead.
units.literal: In the fourth year he became General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xuzhou and was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng, but did not take up the post; soon after he was appointed Palace Attendant and Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 太清初，又爲使持節、都督廣越交桂等十三州諸軍事、征南將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，行至雷首，遇疾卒，時年五十八。
units.en: Early in Taiqing he returned to Guangzhou with the same vast command, reached Leishou, sickened, and died at fifty-eight.
units.literal: At the opening of Taiqing he again became Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in the thirteen provinces of Guang, Yue, Jiao, Gui, and others, General Who Campaigns South, Inspector General Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou; he reached Leishou, fell ill, and died at the age of fifty-eight.

units.zh: 景仲封枝江縣公，邑千戶，拜侍中、右衛將軍。
units.en: Jingzhong received Zhijiang duke with a thousand households and posts as Palace Attendant and General of the Right Guard.
units.literal: Jingzhong was enfeoffed Duke of Zhijiang county with a fief of one thousand households and appointed Palace Attendant and General of the Right Guard.

units.zh: 大通三年，增封，並前爲二千戶，仍賜女樂一部。
units.en: Datong year 3 enlarged his fief to two thousand households and gave him a company of palace musicians.
units.literal: In the third year of Datong his enfeoffment was increased, bringing the total to two thousand households, and he was also granted a troupe of female musicians.

units.zh: 出爲持節、都督廣、越等十三州諸軍事、宣惠將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
units.en: He then took staff authority over Guang and Yue as General Who Proclaims Grace, Pacifier of Yue, and Guangzhou inspector.
units.literal: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Guang, Yue, and the other provinces, General Who Proclaims Grace, Inspector General Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 大同中，徵侍中、左衛將軍。
units.en: During Datong he was recalled as Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard.
units.literal: In Datong he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard.

units.zh: 兄景隆後爲廣州刺史。
units.en: His elder brother Jinglong later became Inspector of Guangzhou.
units.literal: His elder brother Jinglong later became Inspector of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 侯景作亂，以景仲元氏之族，遣信誘之，許奉爲主。
units.en: When Hou Jing rebelled, he sent word to entice Jingzhong, a member of the Yuan imperial clan, promising to install him as ruler.
units.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, because Jingzhong was of the Yuan clan, Jing sent envoys to entice him, promising to set him up as sovereign.

units.zh: 景仲乃舉兵，將下應景。
units.en: Jingzhong mobilized to link arms with Hou Jing from the south.
units.literal: Jingzhong thereupon raised troops, intending to march down and join Jing.

units.zh: 會西江督護陳霸先與成州刺史王懷明等起兵攻之，霸先徇其衆曰：「朝廷以元景仲與賊連從，謀危社稷，今使曲江公勃爲刺史，鎮撫此州。」
units.en: Chen Baxian of the West River commandery and Chengzhou inspector Wang Huaiming rose against him. Baxian told the soldiers, “The throne judges Yuan Jingzhong in league with Hou Jing and a danger to the realm. Duke Bo of Qujiang is coming as your new inspector.”
units.literal: Just then Chen Baxian, Supervisor of the West River, and Wang Huaiming, Inspector of Chengzhou, among others, raised forces to attack him; Baxian proclaimed to the troops: “The court holds that Yuan Jingzhong has marched with the bandits and plots against the altars of state; it now sends Bo, Duke of Qujiang, as inspector to pacify this province.”

units.zh: 衆聞之，皆棄甲而散，景仲乃自縊而死。
units.en: At the news his army melted away; Jingzhong strangled himself.
units.literal: When the crowd heard this, all cast off armor and scattered; Jingzhong then hanged himself.

units.zh: 元樹，字君立，亦魏之近屬也。
units.en: Yuan Shu, styled Junli, was another near kinsman of the Wei imperial house.
units.literal: Yuan Shu, courtesy name Junli, was likewise a close kinsman of Wei.

units.zh: 祖獻文帝。
units.en: His grandfather was Emperor Xianwen.
units.literal: His grandfather was Emperor Xianwen.

units.zh: 父僖，咸陽王。
units.en: His father Xi held the title Prince of Xianyang.
units.literal: His father Xi was Prince of Xianyang.

units.zh: 樹仕魏爲宗正卿，屬尒朱榮亂，以天監八年歸國，封爲鄴王，邑二千戶，拜散騎常侍。
units.en: In Wei he was Director of the Imperial Clan; after Erzhu Rong’s upheaval he defected in Tianjian year 8, was made Prince of Ye with two thousand households, and became Regular Attendant.
units.literal: Shu served Wei as Director of the Imperial Clan; when Erzhu Rong’s turmoil broke out, he came over in the eighth year of Tianjian, was enfeoffed Prince of Ye with a fief of two thousand households, and appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 普通六年，應接元法僧還朝，遷使持節、督郢司霍三州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、郢州刺史，增封並前爲三千戶。
units.en: Putong year 6 saw him escort Faseng home, then take staff command over Ying, Si, and Huo as General of Cloudlike Pennants and Yingzhou inspector, with his fief raised to three thousand households.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Putong he went out to meet Yuan Faseng on his return to court, was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Ying, Si, and Huo, General of Cloudlike Pennants, and Inspector of Yingzhou, and his enfeoffment was increased to three thousand households in all.

units.zh: 討南蠻賊，平之，加散騎常侍、安西將軍，又增邑五百戶。
units.en: A campaign against southern rebels succeeded; he gained Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and five hundred more households.
units.literal: He campaigned against southern barbarian bandits, pacified them, was promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the West, and his fief was again increased by five hundred households.

units.zh: 中大通二年，徵侍中、鎮右將軍。
units.en: Zhongdatong year 2 recalled him as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Right.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Right.

units.zh: 四年，爲使持節，鎮北將軍，都督北討諸軍事，加鼓吹一部以伐魏，攻魏譙城，拔之。
units.en: Year 4 gave him staff authority as General Who Guards the North and commander of the northern expedition, with war drums and orders against Wei; he stormed and seized Qiao.
units.literal: In the fourth year he became Bearer of the Staff, General Who Guards the North, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Northern Campaign Military Affairs, was granted a suite of war drums, and campaigned against Wei; he attacked the Wei city of Qiao and took it.

units.zh: 會魏將獨孤如願來援，遂圍樹，城陷被執，發憤卒于魏，時年四十八。
units.en: Dugu Ruyuan came to relieve the city and then besieged Shu. When the city fell, Shu was captured; he died in Wei of pent-up indignation at forty-eight.
units.literal: The Wei general Dugu Ruyuan came to the rescue, then besieged Shu; the city fell and he was captured; he died of grief in Wei at the age of forty-eight.

units.zh: 子貞，大同中，求隨魏使崔長謙至鄴葬父，還拜太子舍人。
units.en: His son Zhen, in Datong, traveled north with envoy Cui Changqian to bury his father at Ye, came back, and became Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: His son Zhen, in Datong, asked to follow the Wei envoy Cui Changqian to Ye to bury his father, then returned and was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 太清初，侯景降，請元氏戚屬，願奉爲主，詔封貞爲咸陽王，以天子之禮遣還北，會景敗而返。
units.en: Early Taiqing brought Hou Jing’s offer to crown a Yuan prince; Zhen was made Prince of Xianyang and sent north in state, but Hou Jing’s fall sent him home again.
units.literal: At the opening of Taiqing, when Hou Jing surrendered, he asked for a Yuan kinsman to set up as sovereign; an edict enfeoffed Zhen Prince of Xianyang and sent him north with imperial ceremony, but Jing was defeated before he could go and he returned.

units.zh: 元願達，亦魏之支庶也。
units.en: Yuan Yuanda, too, came from a Wei cadet branch.
units.literal: Yuan Yuanda was likewise a collateral of Wei.

units.zh: 祖明元帝。
units.en: His grandfather was Emperor Mingyuan.
units.literal: His grandfather was Emperor Mingyuan.

units.zh: 父樂平王。
units.en: His father held the title Prince of Leping.
units.literal: His father was Prince of Leping.

units.zh: 願達仕魏爲中書令、郢州刺史。
units.en: In Wei he was Director of the Secretariat and inspector of Yingzhou.
units.literal: Yuanda served Wei as Director of the Secretariat and Inspector of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 普通中，大軍北伐，攻義陽，願達舉州獻款，詔封樂平公，邑千戶，賜甲第女樂。
units.en: During Putong’s northern offensive on Yiyang he handed over his province; the court made him Duke of Leping with a thousand households, a mansion, and musicians.
units.literal: In Putong, during the great northern campaign against Yiyang, Yuanda surrendered the whole province; an edict enfeoffed him Duke of Leping with a fief of one thousand households and granted him a mansion and female musicians.

units.zh: 仍出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督湘州諸軍事、平南將軍、湘州刺史。
units.en: He next went to Xiangzhou with staff authority, Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and the inspector’s seal.
units.literal: He was then sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Xiangzhou, General Who Pacifies the South, and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 中大通二年，徵侍中、太中大夫、翊左將軍。
units.en: Zhongdatong year 2 brought him back as Palace Attendant, Grand Master of the Palace, and General Who Assists the Left.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was summoned as Palace Attendant, Grand Master of the Palace, and General Who Assists the Left.

units.zh: 大同三年，卒，時年五十七。
units.en: He died in Datong year 3 at fifty-seven.
units.literal: In the third year of Datong he died at the age of fifty-seven.

units.zh: 王神念，太原祁人也。
units.en: Wang Shenian came from Qi in Taiyuan commandery.
units.literal: Wang Shenian was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 少好儒術，尤明內典。
units.en: As a youth he studied Confucian texts and delved deep into Buddhist sutras.
units.literal: In youth he loved Confucian learning and was especially versed in Buddhist scriptures.

units.zh: 仕魏起家州主簿，稍遷潁川太守，遂據郡歸款。
units.en: He entered Wei service as a provincial registrar, became Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, then held the commandery and tendered his allegiance to Liang.
units.literal: He began his career in Wei as a provincial registrar, gradually rose to Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, and then held the commandery and tendered his allegiance.

units.zh: 魏軍至，與家屬渡江，封南城縣侯，邑五百戶。
units.en: Wei troops forced him across the Yangzi with his family; Liang enfeoffed him Marquis of Nancheng with five hundred households.
units.literal: When Wei armies arrived, he crossed the river with his household and was enfeoffed Marquis of Nancheng county with a fief of five hundred households.

units.zh: 頃之，除安成內史，又歷武陽、宣城內史，皆著治績。
units.en: He governed Ancheng, then Wuyang and Xuancheng, earning a name for effective rule in each.
units.literal: Soon after he was made Administrator of Ancheng and then served as Administrator of Wuyang and Xuancheng, in each post leaving a record of good governance.

units.zh: 還除太僕卿。
units.en: Recalled to court, he became Director of the Imperial Stud.
units.literal: On return he was made Director of the Imperial Stud.

units.zh: 出爲持節、都督青、冀二州諸軍事、信武將軍、青、冀二州刺史。
units.en: He then took Qing and Ji as staff-bearing area commander, General of Trustworthy Martiality, and dual inspector.
units.literal: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Qing and Ji, General of Trustworthy Martiality, and Inspector of Qing and Ji.

units.zh: 神念性剛正，所更州郡必禁止淫祠。
units.en: Stern and upright, he banned improper cults wherever he served.
units.literal: Shenian was upright and stern by nature; in every province or commandery he held, he forbade licentious shrines.

units.zh: 時青、冀州東北有石鹿山臨海，先有神廟，妖巫欺惑百姓，遠近祈禱，糜費極多。
units.en: On the coast northeast of Qing and Ji stood Stone Deer Mountain, long home to a spirit shrine where shamans bled the people dry with endless offerings.
units.literal: At that time in the northeast of Qing and Ji provinces there was a Stone Deer Mountain facing the sea, with a shrine of old; shamans deceived the people, and prayers came from far and near, wasting wealth beyond measure.

units.zh: 及神念至，便令毀撤，風俗遂改。
units.en: Shenian had the shrine torn down, and the custom died with it.
units.literal: When Shenian arrived, he ordered it destroyed and demolished, and local custom was thereby changed.

units.zh: 普通中，大舉北伐，徵爲右衛將軍。
units.en: Putong’s great northern expedition recalled him as General of the Right Guard.
units.literal: In Putong, during the great northern campaign, he was summoned as General of the Right Guard.

units.zh: 六年，遷使持節、散騎常侍、爪牙將軍，右衛如故。
units.en: Year 6 added staff authority, Regular Attendant, and General of the Talons while he kept the Right Guard.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Talons, while retaining the Right Guard.

units.zh: 遘疾卒，時年七十五。
units.en: Illness took him at seventy-five.
units.literal: He fell ill and died at the age of seventy-five.

units.zh: 詔贈本官、衡州刺史，兼給鼓吹一部。
units.en: The throne honored him with his last ranks plus Hengzhou inspector and a war-drum suite.
units.literal: An edict posthumously granted his former office and the post of Inspector of Hengzhou, with a suite of war drums added.

units.zh: 諡曰壯。
units.en: His posthumous name was Zhuang (“Stalwart”).
units.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuang.

units.zh: 神念少善騎射，旣老不衰，嘗於高祖前手執二刀楯，左右交度，馳馬往來，冠絕羣伍。
units.en: A superb horse-archer even in old age, he once rode before Emperor Wu wielding twin sabers and shields, weaving them left and right at full gallop until none in the host could match him.
units.literal: Shenian had been skilled in mounted archery from youth; even in old age he did not decline, and once before Emperor Wu he grasped two sabers and shields in his hands, crossing them left and right as he charged back and forth on horseback, surpassing the whole company.

units.zh: 時復有楊華者，能作驚軍騎，並一時妙捷，高祖深歎賞之。
units.en: Yang Hua, who could startle an army with his horsemanship, shared the spotlight; the emperor delighted in both men.
units.literal: At the time there was also Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry maneuvers; both were marvels of agility for their age, and Emperor Wu deeply admired them.

units.zh: 子尊業，仕至太僕卿。
units.en: His son Zunye reached Director of the Imperial Stud.
units.literal: His son Zunye rose to Director of the Imperial Stud.

units.zh: 卒，贈信威將軍、青、冀二州刺史，鼓吹一部。
units.en: After his death he received General of Trustworthy Prestige, the Qing-Ji inspectorate, and war drums.
units.literal: On death he was posthumously granted General of Trustworthy Prestige and Inspector of Qing and Ji, with a suite of war drums.

units.zh: 次子僧辯，別有傳。
units.en: His second son Sengbian is treated in another chapter.
units.literal: The second son, Sengbian, has a separate biography.

units.zh: 楊華，武都仇池人也。
units.en: Yang Hua came from Chouchi in Wudu.
units.literal: Yang Hua was a native of Chouchi in Wudu.

units.zh: 父大眼，爲魏名將。
units.en: His father Yang Dayan was one of Wei’s great commanders.
units.literal: His father Dayan was a famed general of Wei.

units.zh: 華少有勇力，容貌雄偉，魏胡太后逼通之，華懼及禍，乃率其部曲來降。
units.en: Young, strong, and striking in looks, he fled Wei after Empress Dowager Hu forced herself on him, bringing his household guard south.
units.literal: Hua in youth had courage and strength, a heroic bearing; Empress Dowager Hu of Wei forced him into intimacy; Hua, fearing disaster, led his personal troops to surrender.

units.zh: 胡太后追思之不能已，爲作《楊白華歌辭》，使宮人晝夜連臂蹋足歌之，辭甚悽惋焉。
units.en: Hu could not forget him and wrote the “Yang Baihua” lyrics, set palace women to sing them ceaselessly, hand in hand, stamping the measure—the song was heartbreakingly sad.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager could not stop longing for him and composed the song lyrics “Yang Baihua,” ordering palace women day and night to link arms, stamp their feet, and sing it—the words were exceedingly mournful.

units.zh: 華後累征伐，有戰功，歷官太僕卿，太子左衛率，封益陽縣侯。
units.en: He fought in many campaigns, became Director of the Imperial Stud and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard, and was made Marquis of Yiyang.
units.literal: Hua later took part repeatedly in campaigns and won merit, rising through Director of the Imperial Stud and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang county.

units.zh: 太清中，侯景亂，華欲立志節，妻子爲賊所擒，遂降之，卒於賊。
units.en: Taiqing’s Hou Jing rebellion found him wanting to stand firm until bandits seized his family; he submitted and died in their camp.
units.literal: In Taiqing, when Hou Jing rebelled, Hua wished to hold to integrity, but his wife and children were seized by the bandits, so he surrendered and died among them.

units.zh: 羊侃字祖忻，泰山梁甫人，漢南陽太守續之裔也。
units.en: Yang Kan, styled Zuxin, of Liangfu in Taishan, traced his line to Han’s Yang Xu, grand administrator of Nanyang.
units.literal: Yang Kan, courtesy name Zuxin, was a native of Liangfu in Taishan, a descendant of Yang Xu, Grand Administrator of Nanyang in Han.

units.zh: 祖規，宋武帝之臨徐州，辟祭酒從事、大中正。
units.en: His grandfather Gui was recruited as Libationer-Attendant and Grand Rectifier when the future Emperor Wu of Song governed Xuzhou.
units.literal: His grandfather Gui, when the future Emperor Wu of Song governed Xuzhou, was recruited as Libationer-Attendant and Grand Rectifier.

units.zh: 會薛安都舉彭城降北，規由是陷魏，魏授衛將軍、營州刺史。
units.en: Xue Andu’s surrender of Pengcheng to Northern Wei left Gui on the wrong side of the line; Wei made him General of the Guard and Yingzhou inspector.
units.literal: When Xue Andu raised Pengcheng and went over to the north, Gui was thereby trapped in Wei; Wei appointed him General of the Guard and Inspector of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 父祉，魏侍中，金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: His father Zhi held Wei’s Palace Attendant and golden Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: His father Zhi was Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Ornament in Wei.

units.zh: 侃少而瑰偉，身長七尺八寸，雅愛文史，博涉書記，尤好《左氏春秋》及《孫吳兵法》。
units.en: Even young he was imposing, seven feet eight inches tall; he loved literature and history, read widely, and especially favored the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and the military methods of Sun and Wu.
units.literal: Kan from youth was magnificent in bearing, seven feet eight inches in height, fond of letters by nature, broadly versed in records and documents, and especially loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn and the Art of War of Sun and Wu.

units.zh: 弱冠隨父在梁州立功。
units.en: At twenty he campaigned with his father in Liangzhou and earned distinction.
units.literal: At twenty he followed his father in Liangzhou and won merit.

units.zh: 魏正光中，稍爲別將。
units.en: Under Wei’s Zhengguang era he rose to independent command.
units.literal: In Zhengguang of Wei he gradually became a separate commander.

units.zh: 時秦州羌有莫遮念生者，據州反，稱帝，仍遣其弟天生率衆攻陷岐州，遂寇雍州。
units.en: Qinzhou’s Qiang leader Mo Zhaoniansheng rebelled, crowned himself, and sent his brother Tiansheng to seize Qi Province and raid Yong.
units.literal: At that time among the Qiang of Qinzhou, Mo Zhaoniansheng held the province in revolt, declared himself emperor, and still sent his younger brother Tiansheng at the head of the host to take Qi Province and then raid Yong Province.

units.zh: 侃爲偏將，隸蕭寶夤往討之，潛身巡緌，伺射天生，應弦卽倒，其衆遂潰。
units.en: Serving under Xiao Baoyin, Kan stole along the front, drew on Tiansheng, and dropped him with one arrow; the rebels broke.
units.literal: Kan was a subordinate general under Xiao Baoyin on the punitive expedition; he went in secret along the line of battle, watched for a shot at Tiansheng, and when the arrow flew Tiansheng fell at once and the host collapsed.

units.zh: 以功遷使持節、征東大將軍、東道行臺，領泰山太守，進爵鉅平侯。
units.en: The victory won him staff authority, General Who Campaigns East, eastern commissioner, Taishan administrator, and the marquisate of Juping.
units.literal: For merit he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns East, Eastern Expedition Commissioner, concurrent Grand Administrator of Taishan, and advanced in rank to Marquis of Juping.

units.zh: 初，其父每有南歸之志，常謂諸子曰：「人生安可久淹異域，汝等可歸奉東朝。」
units.en: His father had long wished to return south and often told his sons, “How can a man remain long in a foreign land? You should return and serve the Eastern Court.”
units.literal: Earlier his father had often wished to return south and would regularly tell his sons: “How can a man long linger in a foreign land? You should go home and serve the Eastern Court.”

units.zh: 侃至是將舉河濟以成先志。
units.en: Kan now meant to stir the Yellow and Ji region to honor that vow.
units.literal: Kan now intended to raise the Yellow and Ji rivers to fulfill that earlier wish.

units.zh: 兗州刺史羊敦，侃從兄也，密知之，據州拒侃。
units.en: His cousin Yang Dun, Yanzhou inspector, got wind of the plot and barred the province against him.
units.literal: Yang Dun, Inspector of Yanzhou, was Kan’s paternal cousin; he learned of it in secret and held the province to resist Kan.

units.zh: 侃乃率精兵三萬襲之，弗剋，仍築十餘城以守之。
units.en: Kan hit him with thirty thousand elite troops, failed to take him, and ringed the land with a dozen fortified camps.
units.literal: Kan then led thirty thousand picked troops to strike him, could not overcome him, and still built more than ten walled camps to hold him.

units.zh: 朝廷賞授，一與元法僧同。
units.en: Liang treated him with the same honors it had given Yuan Faseng.
units.literal: The court’s rewards and appointments were the same as for Yuan Faseng.

units.zh: 遣羊鴉仁、王弁率軍應接，李元履運給糧仗。
units.en: Yang Yaren and Wang Bian marched to his aid while Li Yuanlü ran supplies.
units.literal: Yang Yaren and Wang Bian led armies to support him; Li Yuanlü transported grain and weapons.

units.zh: 魏帝聞之，使授侃驃騎大將軍、司徒、泰山郡公，長爲兗州刺史，侃斬其使者以徇。
units.en: Wei tried to buy him with General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Works, Duke of Taishan, and permanent Yanzhou inspector; Kan killed the envoy and exposed the head.
units.literal: When the Wei emperor heard of it, he sent orders appointing Kan General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Works, Duke of Taishan commandery, and long-term Inspector of Yanzhou; Kan beheaded the envoy and displayed the head.

units.zh: 魏人大駭，令僕射于暉率衆數十萬，及高歡、尒朱陽都等相繼而至，圍侃十餘重，傷殺甚衆。
units.en: Wei sent Yu Hui with hundreds of thousands, then Gao Huan and Erzhu Yangdu in waves, wrapping Kan in layer after layer of siege and slaughter.
units.literal: The Wei were greatly alarmed and sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Hui at the head of several hundred thousand men, while Gao Huan, Erzhu Yangdu, and others came in succession, surrounding Kan in more than a dozen rings and inflicting heavy casualties.

units.zh: 柵中矢盡，南軍不進，乃夜潰圍而出，且戰且行，一日一夜乃出魏境。
units.en: When arrows failed and southern relief stalled, he burst out at night, fighting nonstop for a day and a night before he crossed the border.
units.literal: Arrows in the stockade ran out and the southern armies did not advance; he then broke out by night, fighting as he went, and only after a day and a night did he leave Wei territory.

units.zh: 至渣口，衆尚萬餘人，馬二千匹，將入南，士卒並竟夜悲歌。
units.en: At Zhakou ten thousand men and two thousand horses remained; on the eve of crossing south, his troops keened through the night.
units.literal: At Zhakou he still had more than ten thousand men and two thousand horses; about to enter the south, the soldiers all sang laments through the night.

units.zh: 侃乃謝曰：「卿等懷土，理不能見隨，幸適去留，於此別異。」
units.en: Kan told them, “You long for home and need not follow me—stay or go; this is where we divide.”
units.literal: Kan then said in farewell: “You cherish your homeland and cannot rightly follow me; go or stay as you please—here we part.”

units.zh: 因各拜辭而去。
units.en: Each man bowed farewell and went his way.
units.literal: Thereupon each bowed in leave and departed.

units.zh: 侃以大通三年至京師，詔授使持節、散騎常侍、都督瑕丘征討諸軍事、安北將軍、徐州刺史，并其兄默及三弟忱、給、元，皆拜爲刺史。
units.en: He entered the capital in Datong year 3 with staff authority, Regular Attendant, Xiqiu campaign commander, General Who Pacifies the North, and Xuzhou inspector—and his brother Mo and brothers Chen, Ji, and Yuan were all made inspectors too.
units.literal: Kan reached the capital in the third year of Datong; an edict appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Area Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs for the Xiqiu Campaign, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Xuzhou, and his elder brother Mo and three younger brothers Chen, Ji, and Yuan were all appointed inspectors.

units.zh: 尋以侃爲都督北討諸軍事，出頓日城，會陳慶之失律，停進。
units.en: He was soon named northern expedition commander and took post at Richeng, but Chen Qingzhi’s breach of orders stopped the march.
units.literal: Soon Kan was made Area Commander-in-Chief of all Northern Expedition forces, encamped at Richeng; when Chen Qingzhi lost discipline, the advance halted.

units.zh: 其年，詔以爲持節、雲麾將軍、青、冀二州刺史。
units.en: The same year brought staff authority, General of the Cloud Banner, and the Qing-Ji inspectorate.
units.literal: That year an edict appointed him Bearer of the Staff, General of the Cloud Banner, and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.

units.zh: 中大通四年，詔爲使持節、都督瑕丘諸軍事、安北將軍、兗州刺史，隨太尉元法僧北討。
units.en: Zhongdatong year 4 made him full staff bearer, Xiqiu area commander, General Who Pacifies the North, and Yanzhou inspector on Yuan Faseng’s northern campaign.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was appointed Full Staff Bearer, Area Commander of Xiqiu forces, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Yanzhou, to join the Grand Commandant Yuan Faseng on the northern campaign.

units.zh: 法僧先啓云：「與侃有舊，願得同行。」
units.en: Faseng had already written, “Kan and I are old friends—I ask to campaign at his side.”
units.literal: Faseng had first memorialized: “I have old ties with Kan and wish to march together.”

units.zh: 高祖乃召侃問方略，侃具陳進取之計。
units.en: The emperor called Kan in for strategy, and Kan set out a complete plan of attack.
units.literal: The High Ancestor then summoned Kan to ask strategy; Kan laid out a full plan of conquest.

units.zh: 高祖因曰：「知卿願與太尉同行。」
units.en: The emperor said, “I know you want to march with the Grand Commandant.”
units.literal: The High Ancestor then said: “I know you wish to go with the Grand Commandant.”

units.zh: 侃曰：「臣拔跡還朝，常思效命，然實未曾願與法僧同行。
units.en: Kan answered, “Since I came south I have lived to serve—but I never wanted to travel with Faseng.
units.literal: Kan said: “Your servant, having torn himself from the north to return to court, constantly thinks of giving his life, yet in truth I never wished to go with Faseng.

units.zh: 北人雖謂臣爲吳，南人已呼臣爲虜，今與法僧同行，還是羣類相逐，非止有乖素心，亦使匈奴輕漢。」
units.en: The north calls me a southerner; the south calls me a turncoat. Marching with Faseng would still look like birds of a feather—and teach the barbarians to scorn the Han.”
units.literal: Northerners already call me a Wu man; southerners already call me a barbarian captive—if I now go with Faseng, I am still one flock chasing another, which not only betrays my heart but also makes the Xiongnu despise Han.”

units.zh: 高祖曰：「朝廷今者要須卿行。」
units.en: The emperor said, “The court needs you on this march.”
units.literal: The High Ancestor said: “The court now must have you go.”

units.zh: 乃詔以爲大軍司馬。
units.en: He was named Grand Army Marshal by edict.
units.literal: An edict then appointed him Grand Army Marshal.

units.zh: 高祖謂侃曰；
units.en: The emperor told Kan:
units.literal: The High Ancestor said to Kan:

units.zh: 「軍司馬廢來已久，此段爲卿置之。」
units.en: “Army Marshal has been empty for years—I restore it for you.”
units.literal: “The post of Army Marshal has long been vacant; this time it is set up for you.”

units.zh: 行次官竹，元樹又於譙城喪師。
units.en: At Guanzhu, Yuan Shu lost his force at Qiao.
units.literal: On the march, at Guanzhu, Yuan Shu again lost his army at Qiao.

units.zh: 軍罷，入爲侍中。
units.en: The expedition over, he returned as Palace Attendant.
units.literal: When the campaign ended, he entered court as Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 五年，封高昌縣侯，邑千戶。
units.en: Year 5 made him Marquis of Gaochang, fief of one thousand households.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was enfeoffed Marquis of Gaochang with a fief of a thousand households.

units.zh: 六年，出爲雲麾將軍、晉安太守。
units.en: Year 6 sent him out as General of the Cloud Banner and Jin’an grand administrator.
units.literal: In the sixth year he went out as General of the Cloud Banner and Grand Administrator of Jin’an.

units.zh: 閩越俗好反亂，前後太守莫能止息，侃至討擊，斬其渠帥陳稱、吳滿等，於是郡內肅清，莫敢犯者。
units.en: Min-Yue custom bred revolt; no prior governor had quelled it. Kan struck, killed the chiefs Chen Cheng and Wu Man, and the district went still—none dared raise a hand.
units.literal: The Min and Yue peoples were prone to rebellion; no former administrator had been able to stop it. When Kan arrived he attacked, beheaded the ringleaders Chen Cheng and Wu Man, and thereafter the commandery was quiet and none dared offend.

units.zh: 頃之，徵太子左衛率。
units.en: Soon he was recalled as Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard.
units.literal: Before long he was summoned as Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard.

units.zh: 大同三年，車駕幸樂游苑，侃預宴。
units.en: Datong year 3 brought the emperor to Leyou Gardens; Kan joined the feast.
units.literal: In the third year of Datong the imperial carriage visited the Leyou Gardens; Kan was among those feasted.

units.zh: 時少府奏新造兩刃槊成，長二丈四尺，圍一尺三寸，高祖因賜侃馬，令試之。
units.en: The palace workshops had finished a new double-edged spear—twenty-four feet long, thirteen inches around—and the emperor gave Kan a horse to test it.
units.literal: The Palace Storehouse then reported that a new double-edged spear was complete, twenty-four feet long and thirteen inches in girth; the High Ancestor therefore gave Kan a horse and bade him try it.

units.zh: 侃執槊上馬，左右擊刺，特盡其妙，高祖善之，又制《武宴詩》三十韻以示侃，侃卽席應詔，高祖覽曰：「吾聞仁者有勇，今見勇者有仁，可謂鄒、魯遺風，英賢不絕。」
units.en: Kan mounted, spear in hand, and fenced with flawless grace. Delighted, the emperor wrote thirty rhymes of “Martial Feast Poetry” and Kan answered at once from his seat. The emperor read them and said, “They say the benevolent are brave—today I see brave men who are benevolent. Zou and Lu live on; worthies never die out.”
units.literal: Kan took the spear, mounted, and thrust left and right with consummate skill; the High Ancestor was pleased and also composed thirty rhymes of “Martial Feast Poetry” to show Kan, who answered on the spot at imperial command. The High Ancestor read it and said: “I have heard that the benevolent are brave; now I see that the brave are benevolent—one may say the legacy of Zou and Lu, worthy men unbroken.”

units.zh: 六年，遷司徒左長史。
units.en: Year 6 moved him to Left Chief Clerk under the Minister of Education.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 八年，遷都官尚書。
units.en: Year 8 made him Minister of Justice.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 時尚書令何敬容用事，與之並省，未嘗遊造。
units.en: He Jingrong of the Secretariat held sway; Kan shared his ministry but never visited him.
units.literal: At the time the Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong held power; Kan shared the ministry with him but never paid social calls.

units.zh: 有宦者張僧胤候侃，侃曰：「我床非閹人所坐。」
units.en: The eunuch Zhang Sengyin came to call; Kan said, “My bed is not for eunuchs.”
units.literal: A eunuch, Zhang Sengyin, came to wait on Kan; Kan said: “My couch is not for castrated men to sit on.”

units.zh: 竟不前之，時論美其貞正。
units.en: He would not receive him—and men praised his integrity.
units.literal: In the end, Kan would not receive him; contemporaries praised his uprightness.

units.zh: 九年，出爲使持節、壯武將軍、衡州刺史。
units.en: Year 9 sent him out with full staff, General of Majestic Martiality, and the Hengzhou inspectorate.
units.literal: In the ninth year he went out as Full Staff Bearer, General of Majestic Martiality, and Inspector of Hengzhou.

units.zh: 太清元年，徵爲侍中。
units.en: Taiqing year 1 recalled him as Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was summoned as Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 會大舉北伐，仍以侃爲持節、冠軍，監作韓山堰事，兩旬堰立。
units.en: A great northern campaign put him back as staff bearer and General of the Champion, overseeing the Hanshan dam—finished in twenty days.
units.literal: When a great northern expedition was launched, Kan was again made Bearer of the Staff and General of the Champion to supervise construction of the Hanshan dam; in twenty days the dam stood.

units.zh: 侃勸元帥貞陽侯乘水攻彭城，不納；
units.en: Kan begged the Marquis of Zhenyang to take Pengcheng by flood; the marquis refused.
units.literal: Kan urged the commander-in-chief, the Marquis of Zhenyang, to strike Pengcheng while the waters were high; he would not listen.

units.zh: 旣而魏援大至，侃頻勸乘其遠來可擊，旦日又勸出戰，並不從，侃乃率所領出頓堰上。
units.en: Wei reinforcements swelled; Kan urged hitting them on the march, then urged battle again at dawn—both refused—so he drew his men up on the dam.
units.literal: Before long Wei reinforcements came in force; Kan repeatedly urged striking them while still far from home, and the next day urged battle again—none of it was accepted—so Kan led his own troops to encamp on the dam.

units.zh: 及衆軍敗，侃結陣徐還。
units.en: When the host broke, Kan formed ranks and fell back in order.
units.literal: When the armies were defeated, Kan formed ranks and withdrew slowly.

units.zh: 二年，復爲都官尚書。
units.en: Year 2 restored him as Minister of Justice.
units.literal: In the second year he was again Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 侯景反，攻陷歷陽，高祖問侃討景之策。
units.en: Hou Jing rebelled and seized Liyang; the emperor asked Kan how to crush him.
units.literal: Hou Jing rebelled and took Liyang; the High Ancestor asked Kan for a plan against Jing.

units.zh: 侃曰：「景反跡久見，或容豕突，宜急據採石，令邵陵王襲取壽春。
units.en: Kan said, “Jing’s treachery has been obvious for years. He may still rush like a cornered boar—seize Caishi at once and let the Prince of Shaoling take Shouchun.
units.literal: Kan said: “Jing’s treason has long been plain; he may yet charge like a boar, but we should swiftly hold Caishi and have the Prince of Shaoling seize Shouchun.

units.zh: 景進不得前，退失巢窟，烏合之衆，自然瓦解。」
units.en: Block his advance, cut off his refuge, and this mob will scatter on its own.”
units.literal: If Jing cannot advance and loses his nest, this rabble will break up of itself.”

units.zh: 議者謂景未敢便逼京師，遂寢其策，令侃率千餘騎頓望國門。
units.en: Councillors said Jing would not dare march on the capital yet; the plan died, and Kan was told to hold a thousand horse before the Wang Gate.
units.literal: The debaters said Jing would not dare press the capital at once; the plan was shelved, and Kan was ordered to lead a thousand-odd horsemen to encamp before the Wang Gate.

units.zh: 景至新林，追侃入副宣城王都督城內諸軍事。
units.en: When Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was recalled into the city to serve as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng, who commanded all military affairs within the walls.
units.literal: When Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was recalled into the city to serve as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng, who commanded all military affairs within the walls.

units.zh: 時景旣卒至，百姓競入，公私混亂，無復次第。
units.en: Jing struck too fast; people poured through the gates in chaos, public and private alike.
units.literal: Jing had come so suddenly that commoners rushed in together; public and private were chaos, order gone.

units.zh: 侃乃區分防擬，皆以宗室間之。
units.en: Kan divided the walls into sectors and posted imperial clansmen along each line.
units.literal: Kan then divided sectors for defense, interposing kinsmen of the imperial house throughout.

units.zh: 軍人爭入武庫，自取器甲，所司不能禁，侃命斬數人，方得止。
units.en: Soldiers stormed the armory for arms; officials could not stop them until Kan had several beheaded.
units.literal: Soldiers fought to enter the armory and take weapons for themselves; the officials could not stop them until Kan ordered several men beheaded—then it ceased.

units.zh: 及賊逼城，衆皆恟懼，侃偽稱得射書，云「邵陵王、西昌侯已至近路」。
units.en: As the enemy closed in, panic spread; Kan claimed a captured dispatch: “The Prince of Shaoling and the Marquis of Xichang are almost here.”
units.literal: When the bandits pressed the wall the host panicked; Kan falsely announced he had intercepted a letter saying “the Prince of Shaoling and the Marquis of Xichang have already reached the near road.”

units.zh: 衆乃少安。
units.en: The city steadied a little.
units.literal: The host was somewhat calmed.

units.zh: 賊攻東掖門，縱火甚盛，侃親自距抗，以水沃火，火滅，引弓射殺數人，賊乃退。
units.en: The rebels hit the eastern side gate with fire; Kan met them himself, drowned the flames, shot down several men, and drove them back.
units.literal: The bandits attacked the eastern side gate, setting a great fire; Kan personally resisted, dousing the flames with water; when the fire died he drew his bow and shot several men dead, and the bandits withdrew.

units.zh: 加侍中、軍師將軍。
units.en: He was made Palace Attendant and General of the Army Instructor.
units.literal: He was promoted Palace Attendant and General of the Army Instructor.

units.zh: 有詔送金五千兩，銀萬兩，絹萬匹，以賜戰士，侃辭不受。
units.en: The throne sent five thousand taels of gold, ten thousand of silver, and ten thousand bolts of silk for the troops; Kan refused it.
units.literal: An edict sent five thousand taels of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, and ten thousand bolts of silk to reward the warriors; Kan declined to accept.

units.zh: 部曲千餘人，並私加賞賚。
units.en: His own following of a thousand men he rewarded from his purse.
units.literal: To his personal following of more than a thousand he gave private rewards besides.

units.zh: 賊爲尖頂木驢攻城，矢石所不能制，侃作雉尾炬，施鐵鏃，以油灌之，擲驢上焚之，俄盡。
units.en: The rebels raised pointed wooden “donkeys” proof against shot and stone; Kan devised pheasant-tail torches tipped with iron, oil-soaked, and burned the engines to ash.
units.literal: The bandits built pointed wooden donkeys to assault the wall, which arrows and stones could not stop; Kan made pheasant-tail torches with iron heads, soaked them in oil, and hurled them onto the donkeys to burn them—all were soon consumed.

units.zh: 賊又東西兩面起土山，以臨城，城中震駭，侃命爲地道，潛引其土，山不能立。
units.en: They piled earthworks east and west to dominate the walls; terror rose until Kan tunneled under them and stole their fill—the mounds collapsed.
units.literal: The bandits also raised earthen hills east and west to overlook the wall; the city was shaken with fear until Kan ordered tunnels dug to draw off the earth so the hills could not stand.

units.zh: 賊又作登城樓車，高十餘丈，欲臨射城內，侃曰：「車高緌虛，彼來必倒，可臥而觀之，不勞設備。」
units.en: They built assault towers ten rods high to rain arrows into the city. Kan said, “Too tall, ropes too slack—they will topple. Lie back and watch; no need to prepare.”
units.literal: The bandits also built tower-carts for assault, more than ten rods high, intending to shoot down into the city; Kan said: “The cart is high and the ropes slack—when it comes it must fall; we may watch lying down without troubling to prepare.”

units.zh: 及車動果倒，衆皆服焉。
units.en: The tower moved and fell; the whole city believed him.
units.literal: When the cart moved it indeed fell; all were convinced.

units.zh: 賊旣頻攻不捷，乃築長圍。
units.en: Failing again and again, the rebels threw up a long siege line.
units.literal: The bandits, having attacked repeatedly without success, then built a long encirclement.

units.zh: 朱异、張綰議欲出擊之，高祖以問侃，侃曰：「不可。
units.en: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan urged a sortie; the emperor asked Kan, who said, “No.
units.literal: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan debated sallying out; the High Ancestor asked Kan, and Kan said: “No.

units.zh: 賊多日攻城，旣不能下，故立長圍，欲引城中降者耳。
units.en: They could not breach the walls, so they ring us to breed defectors.
units.literal: The bandits have attacked the city many days and could not take it, so they raise a long encirclement to lure those in the city who would surrender.

units.zh: 今擊之，出人若少，不足破賊，若多，則一旦失利，自相騰踐，門隘橋小，必大致挫衄，此乃示弱，非騁王威也。」
units.en: Sortie with few and we achieve nothing; with many, one slip and we will crush each other at the narrow gates and bridges—a rout that shows weakness, not imperial might.”
units.literal: If we strike now and send few men, we cannot break the bandits; if we send many, one defeat and we will trample one another—the gates are narrow, the bridges small, and we will suffer great rout; this shows weakness, not the spreading of royal majesty.”

units.zh: 不從，遂使千餘人出戰，未及交鋒，望風退走，果以爭橋赴水，死者太半。
units.en: They ignored him and sent out a thousand men; before steel met they ran, fought for the bridge, and more than half drowned.
units.literal: They did not listen and sent a thousand-odd men out; before blades met they fled at sight of the enemy, and in the scramble for the bridge many fell into the water—more than half died.

units.zh: 初，侃長子躭爲景所獲，執來城下示侃，侃謂曰：「我傾宗報主，猶恨不足，豈復計此一子，幸汝早能殺之。」
units.en: Jing had taken Kan’s eldest son Dan and brought him under the wall. Kan called, “I have spent my house for the throne and still call it little—why spare one son? Kill him quickly, I beg you.”
units.literal: Earlier Kan’s eldest son Dan had been taken by Jing and brought beneath the wall to show Kan; Kan said: “I have poured out my clan for the lord and still regret it is not enough—how could I reckon on this one son? I hope you will kill him soon.”

units.zh: 數日復持來，侃謂躭曰：「久以汝爲死，猶復在邪？
units.en: Days later they brought him again. Kan said, “I thought you long dead—still here?
units.literal: Several days later they brought him again; Kan said to Dan: “Long I thought you dead—are you still alive?

units.zh: 吾以身許國，誓死行陣，終不以爾而生進退。」
units.en: My body belongs to the realm; I die in the line. You will never move me.”
units.literal: I have given my body to the state and sworn to die in the ranks; I will never let you govern whether I advance or retreat.”

units.zh: 因引弓射之。
units.en: He drew his bow and shot.
units.literal: Thereupon he drew his bow and shot at him.

units.zh: 賊感其忠義，亦不之害也。
units.en: Even the rebels honored his faith and spared the boy.
units.literal: The bandits were moved by his loyalty and did not harm the son either.

units.zh: 景遣儀同傅士哲呼侃與語曰：「侯王遠來問訊天子，何爲閉距，不時進納？
units.en: Jing sent Fu Shizhe, Compeer of the Third Rank, to parley: “The marquis has come far to greet the Son of Heaven—why shut the gates?
units.literal: Jing sent the Compeer of the Third Rank Fu Shizhe to call Kan and speak: “The marquis has come from afar to inquire after the Son of Heaven—why do you shut him out and not admit him in good time?

units.zh: 尚書國家大臣，宜啓朝廷。」
units.en: You are a pillar of the realm—you should speak to the throne.”
units.literal: The Director is a great minister of the state and ought to report to the court.”

units.zh: 侃曰：「侯將軍奔亡之後，歸命國家，重鎮方城，懸相任寄，何所患苦？
units.en: Kan said, “After your flight you were trusted with a great frontier command—what grievance could you have?
units.literal: Kan said: “After the marquis fled and submitted to the state, he was entrusted with a great frontier post—what hardship could he suffer?

units.zh: 忽致稱兵？
units.en: Why draw swords now?
units.literal: Why suddenly raise arms?

units.zh: 今驅烏合之卒，至王城之下，虜馬飲淮，矢集帝室，豈有人臣而至於此？
units.en: You herd this mob to the capital—barbarian horses at the Huai, arrows at the throne. What subject ever did this?
units.literal: Now you drive this rabble to the royal city; barbarian horses drink at the Huai, arrows cluster at the imperial hall—has any subject ever come to this?

units.zh: 吾荷國重恩，當稟承廟算，以掃大逆耳，不能妄受浮說，開門揖盜。
units.en: I owe the dynasty a great debt; I execute the court’s design and scourge traitors—I will not heed sweet lies and open the gate to thieves.
units.literal: Your servant bears heavy grace from the state and must carry out the temple’s plan to sweep away great treason—I cannot rashly accept empty words and open the gate to welcome robbers.

units.zh: 幸謝侯王，早自爲所。」
units.en: Marquis, see to your own end.”
units.literal: I beg the marquis to look to his own end soon.”

units.zh: 士哲又曰：「侯王事君盡節，不爲朝廷所知，正欲面啓至尊，以除姦佞，旣居戎旅，故帶甲來朝，何謂作逆？」
units.en: Shizhe said, “The marquis served with perfect loyalty and the court misunderstood him. He only wished to see the emperor and purge villains—being in the field he wore armor. How is that treason?”
units.literal: Shizhe also said: “The marquis served his lord with utmost loyalty yet was not understood by the court; he only wished to face the Supreme One and remove wicked ministers—being in the army he therefore came in armor; how is that rebellion?”

units.zh: 侃曰：「聖上臨四海將五十年，聰明叡哲，無幽不照，有何姦佞而得在朝？
units.en: Kan said, “Our sage has ruled fifty years, clear-sighted to the deepest shadow—what villains still sit in court?
units.literal: Kan said: “The sage lord has held the four seas nearly fifty years, bright and wise, nothing hidden in the darkest place—what wicked ministers could remain at court?

units.zh: 欲飾其非，寧無詭說。
units.en: To dress up crime, of course there are clever lies.
units.literal: To gloss over wrong, surely there are crafty words.

units.zh: 且侯王親舉白刃，以向城闕，事君盡節，正若是邪！」
units.en: And you yourself brought naked steel to the palace—is that loyalty?”
units.literal: Moreover the marquis himself raised bare blades against the gate-towers—serving one’s lord with utmost loyalty, is it truly thus?”

units.zh: 士哲無以應，乃曰：「在北之日，久挹風猷，每恨平生，未獲披敘，願去戎服，得一相見。」
units.en: Shizhe was silent, then said, “In the north I long admired you and regretted we never met. Let me doff armor and see you once.”
units.literal: Shizhe had no reply and then said: “In the north I long admired your wind and virtue and always regretted in this life I never met you face to face; I wish to lay aside armor and see you once.”

units.zh: 侃爲之免胄，士哲瞻望久之而去。
units.en: Kan took off his helmet; Shizhe stared a long time and left.
units.literal: Kan removed his helmet for him; Shizhe gazed a long while and departed.

units.zh: 其爲北人所欽慕如此。
units.en: Northerners revered him to that degree.
units.literal: Such was the esteem in which northerners held him.

units.zh: 後大雨，城內土山崩，賊乘之垂入，苦戰不能禁，侃乃令多擲火，爲火城以斷其路，徐於裏築城，賊不能進。
units.en: Heavy rain collapsed the inner earthworks; the enemy poured through. Kan ordered a rain of fire, built a fire-wall across their path, and raised an inner rampart behind it—they could not pass.
units.literal: Later came great rain; the earthen hills within the city collapsed and the bandits exploited it, pressing in; though they fought bitterly they could not hold them back until Kan ordered fire cast in abundance and built a fire-wall to cut their path, then slowly built an inner wall; the bandits could not advance.

units.zh: 十二月，遘疾卒于臺內，時年五十四。
units.en: Twelfth month: illness took him inside the palace at fifty-four.
units.literal: In the twelfth month he fell ill and died within the palace compound, aged fifty-four.

units.zh: 詔給東園秘器，布絹各五百匹，錢三百萬，贈侍中、護軍將軍，鼓吹一部。
units.en: The throne sent the eastern-garden coffin, five hundred bolts of cloth and silk, three million cash, posthumous Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, and a martial pipe band.
units.literal: An edict granted the eastern-garden secret coffin, five hundred bolts each of cloth and silk, three million cash, posthumous appointment as Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, and one set of martial pipes.

units.zh: 侃少而雄勇，膂力絕人，所用弓至十餘石。
units.en: Young he was fierce, strength beyond measure—his bow pulled more than ten piculs.
units.literal: From youth Kan was fierce and brave, with strength beyond other men; the bow he used drew more than ten piculs.

units.zh: 嘗於兗州堯廟蹋壁，直上至五尋，橫行得七跡。
units.en: At Yanzhou’s Yao temple he kicked off a wall, climbed five xun straight up, and walked seven paces along the face.
units.literal: Once at the Yao temple in Yanzhou he kicked off from the wall, climbed straight up five xun, and traversed sideways for seven paces.

units.zh: 泗橋有數石人，長八尺，大十圍，侃執以相擊，悉皆破碎。
units.en: At Si Bridge stood stone figures eight feet tall, ten arm-spans round; Kan smashed them together until all broke.
units.literal: At the Si Bridge there were several stone men, eight feet tall and ten arm-spans around; Kan seized them and struck them against each other until all were shattered.

units.zh: 侃性豪侈，善音律，自造《採蓮》、《棹歌》兩曲，甚有新致。
units.en: Extravagant by nature, skilled in music, he composed “Gathering Lotuses” and “Oar Song”—both strikingly new.
units.literal: Kan by nature was extravagant, skilled in music, and himself composed the two tunes “Gathering Lotuses” and “Oar Song,” very fresh in conception.

units.zh: 姬妾侍列，窮極奢靡。
units.en: Concubines lined his halls in utmost luxury.
units.literal: Concubines attended in ranks, luxury pushed to the limit.

units.zh: 有彈箏人陸太喜，著鹿角爪長七寸。
units.en: His zitherist Lu Taixi wore deer-horn picks seven inches long.
units.literal: There was the zither-player Lu Taixi, who wore deer-horn plectra seven inches long.

units.zh: 儛人張淨琬，腰圍一尺六寸，時人咸推能掌中儛。
units.en: The dancer Zhang Jingwan’s waist measured a foot and six inches—men said she could dance in the palm of one’s hand.
units.literal: The dancer Zhang Jingwan had a waist of one foot six inches; contemporaries all praised her dancing in the palm of the hand.

units.zh: 又有孫荊玉，能反腰帖地，銜得席上玉簪。
units.en: Sun Jingyu could arch backward to the floor and pick up a jade hairpin from the mat with her teeth.
units.literal: There was also Sun Jingyu, who could bend her back to the ground and take up a jade hairpin from the mat with her mouth.

units.zh: 敕賚歌人王娥兒，東宮亦賚歌者屈偶之，並妙盡奇曲，一時無對。
units.en: The emperor gave him the singer Wang Er’er; the heir apparent gave Qu Ou’zhi—both masters of uncanny song, peerless in their time.
units.literal: The throne granted the singer Wang Er’er; the Eastern Palace also granted the singer Qu Ou’zhi—both perfected strange tunes, unmatched in their day.

units.zh: 初赴衡州，於兩艖暃符，起三間通梁水齋，飾以珠玉，加之錦繢，盛設帷屏，陳列女樂，乘潮解纜，臨波置酒，緣塘傍水，觀者填咽。
units.en: Setting out for Hengzhou he moored two great barges at Fuqi, built a three-bay water hall across them in pearl and jade and brocade, filled it with screens, musicians, and concubines, cast off on the tide with wine along the shore—crowds blocked the banks.
units.literal: When he first went to Hengzhou, on two great barges at Fuqi he raised a three-bay water-pavilion spanning the beams, adorned with pearls and jade, hung with brocade, screens and curtains lavishly set, female musicians arrayed; riding the tide they cast off the cables, wine set along the waves, the embankment lined with onlookers, the road choked.

units.zh: 大同中，魏使陽斐，與侃在北嘗同學，有詔令侃延斐同宴。
units.en: In Datong the Wei envoy Yang Fei—Kan’s old northern classmate—was told to share Kan’s table by imperial order.
units.literal: In Datong, the Wei envoy Yang Fei had been Kan’s schoolmate in the north; an edict ordered Kan to extend Fei the same feast.

units.zh: 賓客三百餘人，器皆金玉雜寶，奏三部女樂，至夕，侍婢百餘人，俱執金花燭。
units.en: Three hundred guests drank from gold and jeweled cups while three female ensembles played; at dusk a hundred maids bore golden-flower candles.
units.literal: Guests numbered more than three hundred; vessels were all gold, jade, and mixed treasures; three companies of female musicians performed until evening, and more than a hundred serving maids each held golden-flower candles.

units.zh: 侃不能飲酒，而好賓客交遊，終日獻酬，同其醉醒。
units.en: Kan could not drink but loved company—he toasted all day and matched every guest, drunk or sober.
units.literal: Kan could not drink but loved guests and company; all day he offered toasts, sharing their drunkenness and sobriety.

units.zh: 性寬厚，有器局，嘗南還至漣口，置酒，有客張孺才者，醉於船中失火，延燒七十餘艘，所燔金帛不可勝數。
units.en: Broad and magnanimous, he once feasted at Lian mouth on the way south; a guest, Zhang Rucai, drunk aboard set a fire that burned seventy boats and uncounted gold and silk.
units.literal: He was generous in nature and had breadth of bearing; once returning south he reached Lian mouth and set out wine; a guest, Zhang Rucai, drunk in the boat set a fire that spread to more than seventy vessels, gold and silk burned beyond counting.

units.zh: 侃聞之，都不掛意，命酒不輟。
units.en: Kan heard and never broke stride—wine kept flowing.
units.literal: When Kan heard of it he paid no heed and ordered wine without pause.

units.zh: 孺才慚懼，自逃匿，侃慰喻使還，待之如舊。
units.en: Rucai fled in shame; Kan coaxed him back and treated him as ever.
units.literal: Rucai, ashamed and afraid, fled into hiding; Kan comforted him and had him return, treating him as before.

units.zh: 第三子鶤。
units.en: His third son was Kun.
units.literal: The third son was Kun.

units.zh: 鶤字子鵬。
units.en: Kun, styled Zipeng.
units.literal: Kun, courtesy name Zipeng.

units.zh: 隨侃臺內，城陷，竄於陽平。
units.en: He followed Kan inside the palace; when the city fell he hid at Yangping.
units.literal: He followed Kan within the palace compound; when the city fell he hid at Yangping.

units.zh: 侯景呼還，待之甚厚。
units.en: Hou Jing called him back and favored him richly.
units.literal: Hou Jing summoned him back and treated him very generously.

units.zh: 及景敗，鶤密圖之，乃隨其東走。
units.en: When Jing fell, Kun plotted in secret and followed him east.
units.literal: When Jing was defeated, Kun secretly plotted against him and went east with him.

units.zh: 景于松江戰敗，惟餘三舸，下海欲向蒙山。
units.en: Jing lost on the Song River with three boats left and put to sea for Mengshan.
units.literal: Jing was defeated on the Song River and had only three boats left; he went downriver intending to make for Mengshan.

units.zh: 會景倦晝寢，鶤語海師：「此中何處有蒙山！
units.en: Jing fell asleep at midday; Kun told the pilot, “There is no Mengshan here—
units.literal: Jing, weary, napped by day; Kun spoke to the sea pilot: “Where is there any Mengshan in these waters!

units.zh: 汝但聽我處分。」
units.en: do as I say.”
units.literal: You need only obey my orders.”

units.zh: 遂直向京口。
units.en: They bore straight for Jingkou.
units.literal: They then headed straight for Jingkou.

units.zh: 至胡豆洲，景覺，大驚，問岸上人，云「郭元建猶在廣陵」，景大喜，將依之。
units.en: At Hudou Isle Jing woke in panic and hailed the bank: “Guo Yuanjian still holds Guangling”—Jing was overjoyed and meant to go to him.
units.literal: At Hudou Isle, Jing woke, greatly alarmed, and asked people on the shore, who said, “Guo Yuanjian is still at Guangling”; Jing rejoiced and meant to join him.

units.zh: 鶤拔刀叱海師，使向京口。
units.en: Kun bared his blade and drove the pilot toward Jingkou.
units.literal: Kun drew his sword and shouted at the sea pilot to steer for Jingkou.

units.zh: 景欲透水，鶤抽刀斫之，景乃走入船中，以小刀抉船，鶤以槊入刺殺之。
units.en: Jing tried to swim clear; Kun hacked at him. Jing fled into the cabin and picked at the planking with a knife—Kun ran him through with a spear.
units.literal: Jing tried to slip overboard; Kun struck with his blade. Jing ran into the hold and gouged the hull with a small knife; Kun thrust in with a spear and killed him.

units.zh: 世祖以鶤爲持節、通直散騎常侍、都督青、冀二州諸軍事、明威將軍、青州刺史，封昌國縣公，邑二千戶，賜錢五百萬，米五千石，布絹各一千匹，又領東陽太守。
units.en: Emperor Yuan gave Kun staff authority, Regular Attendant, Qing-Ji area command, General of Bright Awe, and Qingzhou inspector; made him Duke of Changguo, two thousand households; five million cash, five thousand piculs of grain, a thousand bolts each of cloth and silk; and Grand Administrator of Dongyang besides.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan made Kun Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Area Commander of all military affairs for Qing and Ji provinces, General of Bright Awe, and Inspector of Qingzhou; enfeoffed him Duke of the State of Changguo with a fief of two thousand households; granted five million cash, five thousand piculs of grain, and a thousand bolts each of cloth and silk; and he also held the post of Grand Administrator of Dongyang.

units.zh: 征陸納，加散騎常侍。
units.en: Kun campaigned against Lu Na and received the additional title of Regular Attendant.
units.literal: Kun campaigned against Lu Na and was given the additional title of Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 平峽中，除西晉州刺史。
units.en: The gorges pacified, he became Western Jinzhou inspector.
units.literal: When the mid-Yangzi gorges were pacified he was appointed Inspector of Western Jinzhou.

units.zh: 破郭元建於東關，遷使持節、信武將軍、東晉州刺史。
units.en: Kun defeated Guo Yuanjian at Dong Pass and was promoted to Full Staff Bearer, General of Trustworthy Valor, and Inspector of Eastern Jinzhou.
units.literal: After Kun defeated Guo Yuanjian at Dong Pass, he was promoted to Full Staff Bearer, General of Trustworthy Valor, and Inspector of Eastern Jinzhou.

units.zh: 承聖三年，西魏圍江陵，鶤赴援不及，從王僧愔征蕭勃於嶺表。
units.en: In 554, Western Wei besieged Jiangling. Kun arrived too late to help and then accompanied Wang Sengyin against Xiao Bo in Lingnan.
units.literal: In the third year of Chengsheng, Western Wei besieged Jiangling; Kun could not reach them in time and followed Wang Sengyin on the campaign against Xiao Bo in Lingnan.

units.zh: 聞太尉僧辯敗，乃還，爲侯瑱所破，於豫章遇害，時年二十八。
units.en: When word came that Grand Marshal Sengbian had fallen, Kun turned back. Hou Tian routed him, and Kun was killed at Yuzhang at the age of twenty-eight.
units.literal: Hearing that Grand Marshal Sengbian had been defeated, Kun turned back; Hou Tian defeated him, and he was killed at Yuzhang, aged twenty-eight.

units.zh: 羊鴉仁，字孝穆，太山鉅平人也。
units.en: Yang Yaren, styled Xiaomu, came from Juping in Taishan.
units.literal: Yang Yaren, styled Xiaomu, was a man of Juping in Taishan commandery.

units.zh: 少驍果有膽力，仕郡爲主簿。
units.en: Young he was bold and strong and served the commandery as recorder.
units.literal: In youth he was fierce and daring, with courage and strength; he served the commandery as chief clerk.

units.zh: 普通中，率兄弟自魏歸國，封廣晉縣侯。
units.en: In Putong he brought his brothers south from Wei and was made Marquis of Guangjin.
units.literal: In the Putong era he led his brothers back from Wei to the homeland and was enfeoffed Marquis of Guangjin county.

units.zh: 征伐青、齊間，累有功績，稍遷員外散騎常侍、歷陽太守。
units.en: Fighting in Qing and Qi he won honors, rising to Extraordinary Attendant and Liyang grand administrator.
units.literal: In campaigns between Qing and Qi he accumulated merit and was gradually promoted to Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Administrator of Liyang.

units.zh: 中大通四年，爲持節、都督譙州諸軍事、信威將軍、譙州刺史。
units.en: Zhongdatong year 4 made him staff bearer, Qiao area commander, General of Trustworthy Awe, and Qiaozhou inspector.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was made Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of all military affairs for Qiao province, General of Trustworthy Awe, and Inspector of Qiaozhou.

units.zh: 大同七年，除太子左衛率，出爲持節、都督南、北司、豫、楚四州諸軍事、輕車將軍、北司州刺史。
units.en: Datong year 7 brought Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard, then staff bearer over southern and northern Si, Yu, and Chu, General of Light Chariots, and Northern Sizhou inspector.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Datong he was appointed Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard, then went out as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of all military affairs for the Southern and Northern Si, Yu, and Chu provinces, General of Light Chariots, and Inspector of Northern Sizhou.

units.zh: 侯景降，詔鴉仁督士州刺史桓和之、仁州刺史湛海珍等精兵三萬，趨懸瓠應接景，仍爲都督豫司淮冀殷應西豫等七州諸軍事、司豫二州刺史，鎮懸瓠。
units.en: When Hou Jing submitted, Yaren was told to lead Huan Hezhi of Shizhou, Zhan Haizhen of Renzhou, and thirty thousand picked men to Xuanhu to meet Jing—and to command seven provinces from Yu to Western Yu as Si-Yu inspector, based at Xuanhu.
units.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered, an edict ordered Yaren to supervise Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Shizhou, Zhan Haizhen, Inspector of Renzhou, and others with thirty thousand elite troops to hurry to Xuanhu to link with Jing; he also served as Area Commander of all military affairs for the seven provinces of Yu, Si, Huai, Ji, Yin, Ying, and Western Yu, and as Inspector of Si and Yu provinces, stationed at Xuanhu.

units.zh: 會侯景敗於渦陽，魏軍漸逼，鴉仁恐糧運不繼，遂還北司，上表陳謝。
units.en: Jing lost at Woyang and Wei closed in; Yaren, afraid grain would not follow, pulled back to Northern Si and apologized by memorial.
units.literal: Jing was defeated at Woyang and Wei forces pressed closer; fearing his supply line would fail, Yaren returned to Northern Si and submitted a memorial apologizing.

units.zh: 高祖大怒，責之，鴉仁懼，又頓軍於淮上。
units.en: The High Ancestor raged and blamed him; Yaren, afraid, camped again on the Huai.
units.literal: The High Ancestor was furious and rebuked him; Yaren in fear halted his army on the Huai.

units.zh: 及侯景反，鴉仁率所部入援。
units.en: When Jing turned rebel, Yaren marched his command to the rescue.
units.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Yaren led his troops to the capital in relief.

units.zh: 太清二年，景旣背盟，鴉仁乃與趙伯超及南康王會理共攻賊於東府城，反爲賊所敗。
units.en: Taiqing year 2: Jing broke faith; Yaren, Zhao Bochao, and Prince Huili of Nankang struck the rebels at the Eastern Directorate and were beaten in turn.
units.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, after Jing broke the alliance, Yaren joined Zhao Bochao and Prince Huili of Nankang to attack the rebels at the Eastern Directorate compound but was in turn defeated by the rebels.

units.zh: 臺城陷，鴉仁見景，爲景所留，以爲五兵尚書。
units.en: The inner city fell; Yaren presented himself to Jing, who held him and named him Minister of the Five Weapons.
units.literal: When the capital fortress fell, Yaren went to see Jing and was detained by him, appointed Minister of the Five Weapons.

units.zh: 鴉仁常思奮發，謂所親曰：「吾以凡流，受寵朝廷，竟無報效，以答重恩。
units.en: Yaren brooded on a reckoning and told his intimates, “I am nobody, yet the throne raised me—and I have never repaid that debt.
units.literal: Yaren often thought of striking back and told those close to him: “I am but common clay, yet the court favored me, and I have utterly failed to repay that deep grace.

units.zh: 社稷傾危，身不能死，偷生苟免，以至於今。
units.en: The realm crumbled and I would not die; I stole life and slipped away, and so it has gone.
units.literal: The altars tottered and I could not die—I clung to life and escaped, until today.

units.zh: 若以此終，沒有餘憤。」
units.en: If I end like this, I shall die with resentment still unspent.”
units.literal: To end this way leaves every grievance unspent.”

units.zh: 因遂泣下，見者傷焉。
units.en: He wept as he spoke; all who heard were stricken.
units.literal: and he wept; those who saw it were grieved.

units.zh: 三年，出奔江西，其故部曲數百人迎之，將赴江陵，至東莞，爲故北徐州刺史荀伯道諸子所害。
units.en: Year 3 he fled into Jiangxi; a few hundred veterans met him bound for Jiangling—but at Dongguan the sons of ex–Northern Xuzhou inspector Xun Bodao killed him.
units.literal: In the third year he fled west to Jiangxi; several hundred of his old followers welcomed him; he was bound for Jiangling but at Dongguan was murdered by the sons of the former Inspector of Northern Xuzhou, Xun Bodao.

units.zh: 史臣曰：高祖革命受終，光期寶運，威德所漸，莫不懷來，其皆殉難投身，前後相屬。
units.en: The historian writes: The High Ancestor took the throne and lit the age with fortune; his power drew every heart, and men threw themselves into death for the realm in endless succession.
units.literal: The historian writes: The High Ancestor received the mandate in revolution and shone with the fortune of the age; where his power and virtue reached, none failed to come in heart—and they died for the state one after another.

units.zh: 元法僧之徒入國，並降恩遇，位重任隆，擊鐘鼎食，美矣。
units.en: Yuan Faseng and his kind who came south were heaped with favor—heavy office, high rank, bells and tripods at feast: glorious.
units.literal: Yuan Faseng and men like him who entered the realm were all showered with grace, given weighty posts and lofty rank, bell and tripod at table—splendid indeed.

units.zh: 而羊侃、鴉仁值太清之難，並竭忠奉國。
units.en: Yet Kan and Yaren met the Taiqing disaster and gave the state their utmost loyalty.
units.literal: Yet Yang Kan and Yaren met the calamity of Taiqing and both poured out loyalty for the state.

units.zh: 侃則臨危不撓，鴉仁守義殞命，可謂志等松筠，心均鐵石，古之殉節，斯其謂乎！
units.en: Kan never bent under danger; Yaren kept faith and died—wills like pine and bamboo, hearts like iron and stone: the martyrs of old, was it not for such as these?
units.literal: Kan unbent in peril; Yaren kept faith and gave his life—they may be said to match pine and bamboo in will, iron and stone in heart; of the martyrs of old, is this not meant?

units.zh: 十五年，魏東益州刺史元法僧遣子景隆來拒齊師，南安太守皇甫諶及宗範逆擊之，大破魏軍於葭萌，屠十餘城，魏將丘突、王穆等皆降。
units.en: In year fifteen Wei east Yizhou inspector Yuan Faseng sent his son Jinglong against Qi; Nan'an administrator Huangfu Chen and Zongfan counterattacked, crushing the Wei army at Jiameng, sacking more than ten cities; Wei generals Qiu Tu and Wang Mu among others surrendered.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year, Wei East Yizhou Inspector Yuan Faseng sent his son Jinglong to resist Qi's army; Nan'an Administrator Huangfu Chen and Zongfan counterattacked, smashing the Wei host at Jiameng, slaughtering more than ten cities; Wei generals Qiu Tu, Wang Mu, and others all surrendered.

units.zh: 從行臺蕭寶寅討破宛川，俘其民人為奴婢，以美女十人賞蘭根。
units.en: Following Mobile Headquarters Xiao Baoyin, he helped defeat Wanchuan. Captives were made slaves; ten fair women were awarded to Langen as his prize.
units.literal: Following Mobile Headquarters Xiao Baoyin, he defeated Wanchuan; the captive populace were made slaves and bondmaids, and ten fair women were awarded to Langen as reward.

units.zh: 屬秦隴反叛，蕭寶寅敗於涇州，高平虜賊逼岐州，州城民逼囚蘭根降賊。
units.en: When Qin and Long rose in rebellion, Xiao Baoyin was defeated at Jing Province. Gaoping barbarian bandits pressed Qi Province, and townsfolk forced Langen into captivity to surrender to the rebels.
units.literal: As Qin and Long rebelled, Xiao Baoyin was defeated at Jing Province; barbarian bandits of Gaoping pressed Qi Province, and the townsfolk forced and imprisoned Langen to surrender to the rebels.

units.zh: 寶寅至雍州，收輯散亡，兵威復振，城民復斬賊刺史侯莫陳仲和，推蘭根復任。
units.en: Baoyin reached Yong Province, gathered scattered troops, and military prestige revived. The townsfolk beheaded the rebel inspector Hou Mo-Chen Zhonghe and urged Langen to resume office.
units.literal: Baoyin reached Yong Province, gathered scattered troops, and military prestige revived; the townsfolk again beheaded the rebel inspector Hou Mo-Chen Zhonghe and urged Langen to resume his post.

units.zh: 左丞徐爰彈右衞將軍薛安都屬疾不直，免安都官；
units.en: Left Assistant Xu Ai impeached Xue Andu, General of the Right Guards, for claiming illness and not attending duty; Andu was dismissed;
units.literal: Left Assistant Xu Ai impeached Xue Andu, General of the Right Guards, for claiming illness and not attending duty; Andu was removed from office;

units.zh: 齊高祖神武皇帝，姓高名歡，字賀六渾，渤海蓚人也。
units.en: Gaozu Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi bore the surname Gao; his personal name was Huan and his style Heiliuhun. He came from Tiao in Bohai.
units.literal: The Grand Ancestor of Qi, Emperor Shenwu, surname Gao, taboo name Huan, style name Heiliuhun, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.

units.zh: 神武上
units.en: Emperor Shenwu, Part One
units.literal: Emperor Shenwu, Part One

units.zh: 家貧，及聘武明皇后，始有馬，得給鎮為隊主。
units.en: The family was poor, and only after he betrothed Lady Wuming did he acquire a horse and win appointment as squad chief at the garrison.
units.literal: His family was poor; only when he betrothed Empress Wuming did he first have a horse and was able to serve the garrison as squad chief.

units.zh: 神武自隊主轉為函使。
units.en: Gao Huan moved from squad chief to garrison courier.
units.literal: Shenwu advanced from squad chief to courier.

units.zh: 自是乃有澄清天下之志。
units.en: From that day he resolved to set the realm right.
units.literal: From this time he nursed the ambition to cleanse and clarify the realm.

units.zh: 神武旣累世北邊，故習其俗，遂同鮮卑。
units.en: For generations his family had lived on the northern marches, so Gao Huan grew up in frontier ways and lived much like the Xianbei.
units.literal: As for generations his family had been on the northern frontier, Shenwu was accustomed to its customs and came to be as the Xianbei.

units.zh: 六世祖隱，晉玄菟太守。
units.en: In the sixth generation his ancestor Yin had been Administrator of Xuantu under the Jin.
units.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yin served as Administrator of Xuantu under Jin.

units.zh: 湖生四子，第三子謐，仕魏，位至侍御史，坐法徙居懷朔鎮。
units.en: Hu had four sons. The third, Mi, served the Wei court and rose to Attending Censor, but after a legal infraction was banished to live at Huaishuo garrison.
units.literal: Hu had four sons; the third, Mi, served Wei, rose to Attending Censor, and for violating the law was exiled to garrison at Huaishuo.

units.zh: 嘗乘驛過建興，雲霧晝晦，雷聲隨之，半日乃絕，若有神應者。
units.en: Once while riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist darkened the day and thunder rolled after him for half a day, as though heaven itself were answering his passage.
units.literal: Once riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist darkened the day, thunder followed along, and for half a day it did not cease — as if there were a divine response.

units.zh: 為函使六年，每至洛陽，給令史麻祥使。
units.en: For six years as courier he went each time to Luoyang, where he was assigned to the clerk Ma Xiang.
units.literal: For six years as courier, whenever he reached Luoyang he was detailed to the clerk Ma Xiang.

units.zh: 及自洛陽還，傾產以結客。
units.en: On his return from Luoyang he poured out his fortune to gather followers.
units.literal: When he returned from Luoyang, he expended his whole estate to gather clients.

units.zh: 親故怪問之，答曰：「吾至洛陽，宿衛羽林相率焚領軍張彝宅，朝廷懼其亂而不問。
units.en: Kinsmen and friends asked what moved him; he answered, "At Luoyang I saw the Feathered Forest guards burn down the residence of Supreme Commander Zhang Yi in a mob, and the court, fearing worse trouble, never punished them.
units.literal: Relatives and friends wondered and asked him; he replied: "When I reached Luoyang, the palace guards of the Feathered Forest together burned the residence of the supreme commander Zhang Yi, and the court feared their disorder and did not inquire.

units.zh: 見一赤兔，每搏輒逸，遂至回澤。
units.en: They sighted a russet hare that bolted away whenever they closed, and the chase carried them to Huize Marsh.
units.literal: They saw a red hare; each time they closed in it escaped, and they went on as far as Huize Marsh.

units.zh: 澤中有茅屋，將奔入，有狗自屋中出，噬之，鷹兔俱死。
units.en: Near a hut on the marsh the hare was nearly inside when a dog rushed out, tore at it, and killed both hawk and hare.
units.literal: In the marsh there was a thatched hut; as the hare was about to flee into it, a dog came out from the hut and bit it, and hawk and hare both died.

units.zh: 鎮將遼西段長常奇神武貌，謂曰：「君有康濟才，終不徒然。」
units.en: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, the garrison commander, often admired Gao Huan's looks and told him, "You have the talent to heal the realm; you will not end your days obscurely."
units.literal: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, commander of the garrison, often marveled at Shenwu's appearance and said to him: "You possess talent for bringing order and succor; you will not in the end come to nothing."

units.zh: 便以子孫為托。
units.en: And he entrusted his descendants to Gao Huan's care.
units.literal: He thereupon entrusted him with his descendants.

units.zh: 與懷朔省事雲中司馬子如及秀容人劉貴、中山人賈顯智為奔走之友，懷朔戶曹史孫騰、外兵史侯景亦相友結。
units.en: He made running companions of Sima Ziru, affairs clerk at Huaishuo's Yunzhong desk, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan; Sun Teng, the garrison household clerk, and Hou Jing, clerk for external military affairs, joined their circle as well.
units.literal: With Sima Ziru, affairs clerk of Yunzhong at Huaishuo, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan he formed a band of comrades ready to run errands; Sun Teng, household clerk at Huaishuo, and Hou Jing, clerk in external military affairs, also joined in friendship.

units.zh: 劉貴嘗得一白鷹，與神武及尉景、蔡儁、子如、賈顯智等獵於沃野。
units.en: Liu Gui once came by a white hawk and went hunting on the open steppe with Gao Huan, Wei Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi, and the rest.
units.literal: Liu Gui once obtained a white hawk and hunted on the open fields with Shenwu, Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi, and others.

units.zh: 及神武生而皇妣韓氏殂，養於同產姊婿鎮獄隊尉景家。
units.en: When Gao Huan was born his mother Lady Han died, and he was reared in the household of his full elder sister's husband Wei Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.
units.literal: When Shenwu was born the late mother Lady Han died, and he was raised in the home of his uterine elder sister's husband, Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.

units.zh: 長而深沉有大度，輕財重士，為豪俠所宗。
units.en: As a man he was reserved and far-sighted, generous with money and devoted to worthy companions, and the local men of daring looked to him as their leader.
units.literal: When grown he was deep and reserved, possessed of great breadth of mind, lightly regarded wealth and valued men of talent, and was looked to by bold heroes.

units.zh: 目有精光，長頭高顴，齒白如玉，少有人傑表。
units.en: His eyes gleamed, his head was long and his cheekbones high, his teeth white as jade; even in youth he wore the bearing of a man marked for greatness.
units.literal: His eyes had a sharp brilliance; his head was long and cheeks high; his teeth white as jade — in youth he had the countenance of an uncommon man.

units.zh: 詳嘗以肉啖神武，神武性不立食，坐而進之。
units.en: Xiang once fed him meat; Gao Huan, who never ate standing, sat down to accept it.
units.literal: Xiang once offered meat to Shenwu to eat; Shenwu by nature would not eat standing, and so sat to receive it.

units.zh: 因自言善暗相，遍捫諸人皆貴，而指麾俱由神武。
units.en: Declaring herself skilled in reading fate by touch, she passed her hands over each man and pronounced them all destined for rank, yet said every fortune turned on Gao Huan.
